confirmed.evidence: Connection SendCommand IL_00a7 Wait(0), IL_0124 linked-token gate WaitAsync, IL_0269-0273 remaining, IL_0322 pending registration, IL_036d synchronous send, IL_038e cancellable response wait, IL_046a identity removal, IL_0476 release. No pre-send cancellation test on the successful Wait(0) route.

ProcessOneIteration IL_0001 CheckTimeouts precedes IL_0012 receive; response branch calls ResolveRequest. ResolveRequest IL_0009 removes by opcode and IL_0017 completes current TCS. ExpireRequests IL_001a removes exact key/value pair.

DeviceConnection both custom-command wrappers return the DeviceSession task at IL_0011; DeviceSession SendCommand IL_0040 awaits Connection, IL_00cf reads status, IL_013c accepts zero, IL_018c strips status. ResponseCode Ack=0, Nak=1, Unsupported=2.

StopAsync cancels CTS, waits readTask up to two seconds, catches cancellation/timeout, disposes CTS and nulls task/CTS. No requests walk or explicit TCS failure. Reconnect awaits old DisposeAsync then invokes factory; concrete existing factory code constructs new Connection.

scope_notes.detail: remaining is calculated before synchronous SendPacket and reused by WaitAsync after send; it is not reduced again by write/flush time. Active CheckTimeouts separately uses an absolute UTC deadline. Do not advertise a strict end-to-end wall-clock bound from the single remaining value.

Queue CTS and GetElapsedTime/GetUtcNow use injected TimeProvider. The response wait IL signature is WaitAsync(TimeSpan,CancellationToken), without an explicit TimeProvider. The model does not simulate either timer implementation or UTC/monotonic divergence.

Conditional old-response matching requires the same Connection object, same parsed opcode and IsResponse, a registered successor still present after the pre-read timeout sweep, and successful decoding of a genuine response. No actual delayed device response or cross-reconnect occurrence was observed.

Link.stop only marks reading false and checks pending retention; it is not a reader termination simulator. Actual StopAsync has a two-second bounded wait and catches timeout, so return does not alone prove the previous readTask fully stopped. Its pending requests are not explicitly failed by that method.

Unique request strings stand in for TCS identity. Native pair identity includes TCS and deadline. remove_pair is separate from finish/releasing gate in the reviewed revision, avoiding a simulated duplicate finally.

Queued is a returned marker, not a live asynchronous waiter. spent is supplied explicitly; no timer, timeout sweep, wait-queue fairness, synchronous write duration, callback scheduling or serial hardware is simulated. ExpireRequests is represented only by identity-based removal, not its full loop.

Matched opcode plus ACK confirms the software response contract, not valve movement, pressure target, sensor freshness, flash completion or physical byte delivery. Other callers and exact state/lifecycle transitions are outside this limited review.

Already-cancelled free-gate fixture assumes remaining>0, successful synchronous send, and no response completion before the cancellable wait. It does not prescribe the result of every completed-task/cancellation schedule.
